docs.title: Rekit Documentation
docs.text:
rekit gives a terminal — and any Model Context Protocol (MCP) compatible AI agent — a single safe, deterministic front-end for static binary analysis: file triage, strings, IOC extraction, disassembly, APK/DEX, firmware images, JS bundles, PCAPs and headless Ghidra decompilation. It never executes a sample in memory or on disk, and it never invents a result.

Rekit ships as a lightweight, zero-dependency CLI and high-integrity MCP server:

Interface Entrypoint Install / Run Guarantees CLI (Python) rekit.py python3 rekit.py --help Pure stdlib, zero-execution sandbox MCP Server mcp_server.py python3 mcp_server.py Model Context Protocol (JSON-RPC)

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Strictly Read-Only — only verified analysis binaries (readelf, objdump, radare2, jadx, tshark, Ghidra headless) are invoked. Samples are never executed.
  • Nothing Faked — missing system backends explicitly return {"tool_missing": "..."}. Rekit never hallucinates or guesses.
  • Machine-Readable Output — every subcommand accepts --json for direct agent and toolchain ingestion.
  • Bounded Execution — every subprocess enforces hard timeouts and bounded input size caps via REKIT_MAX_BYTES.

docs.title: Quick start in 30 seconds
docs.text:
import json
import subprocess

# Direct triage of binary with clean JSON output
res = subprocess.check_output(["python3", "rekit.py", "triage", "/bin/ls", "--json"])
data = json.loads(res)
print(f"SHA256: {data['sha256']} | Kind: {data['kind']}")

docs.title: Command line (Python)
docs.text:
# Clone and run stdlib CLI
git clone https://github.com/Amz34/rekit.git && cd rekit

# Fast triage: hashes, file format, sections, entropy, packer detection
python3 rekit.py triage /bin/ls --json

# High-entropy strings and indicators of compromise (IOCs)
python3 rekit.py iocs ./firmware_extracted/sys.img

# Function disassembly & headless Ghidra decompilation to C
python3 rekit.py disasm /bin/ls --func main
python3 rekit.py ghidra /bin/ls --out tiny.decompiled.c

docs.title: MCP Server Integration
docs.text:
Connect rekit as an autonomous static analysis tool for Claude Desktop, Cursor, or sovereign agent runtimes:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "rekit": {
      "command": "/usr/bin/python3",
      "args": ["/home/ubuntu/projects/rekit-public/mcp_server.py"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Headless Ghidra Decompilation
docs.text: rekit integrates directly with Ghidra's analyzeHeadless automation pipeline on both x86_64 and ARM64 architectures.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: [Target Binary] ──▶ [rekit CLI/MCP] ──▶ [Ghidra analyzeHeadless] ──▶ [DecompileAll.java] ──▶ [C Pseudocode]

docs.title: Setup & ARM64 Support
docs.text:
Ghidra runs fully natively on Linux ARM64 with JDK 21:

export GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR=/opt/ghidra
python3 rekit.py ghidra /bin/ls --func main

Results are saved to structured markdown or .c files without manual GUI interaction.

docs.title: Architectural Guarantees
docs.text: rekit is built specifically for autonomous agents operating in production environments where accidental malware detonation or hallucinated findings are unacceptable.

docs.title: 1. Strictly Read-Only
docs.text: Under no circumstances does rekit execute an untrusted binary. Only trusted, isolated host tools are shelled out (readelf, objdump, radare2, jadx, tshark, Ghidra).

docs.title: 2. Zero Hallucination
docs.text:
If a system dependency is not installed (e.g. jadx on ARM64), rekit explicitly returns: 

{
  "tool_missing": "jadx"
}
It never guesses or invents findings.

docs.title: 3. Strict Resource Boundaries
docs.text: To protect the host system from fork-bombs and memory exhaustion: - Every child subprocess has an enforced timeout. - File ingestion is capped by REKIT_MAX_BYTES (default 3 GiB).

docs.text:
Add the following block to your claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "rekit": {
      "command": "/usr/bin/python3",

Restart Claude Desktop. The rekit hammer icon will appear in the prompt window, enabling immediate binary triage and static inspection capabilities.

docs.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Quick Start
docs.text: rekit implements an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server over STDIO and HTTP, allowing autonomous coding and security agents to run static analysis directly.

docs.title: Running the MCP Server
docs.text:
# Start STDIO server for agent orchestration
python3 mcp_server.py

docs.title: Available MCP Tools
docs.text:
• rekit_triage: Returns format, hashes, entropy, and packer details.
  • rekit_strings: Extracts filtered strings.
  • rekit_iocs: Returns network and secret indicators.
  • rekit_disasm: Disassembles instructions.
  • rekit_ghidra: Decompiles functions to C via headless Ghidra.

docs.title: MCP Tools & Schema
docs.text: Specifications for all tools exposed by rekit MCP server.

docs.title: Tool: rekit_triage
docs.text:
Arguments: - path (string, required): Absolute path to the binary on disk. - max_bytes (integer, optional): Maximum sample size to inspect.

Response: JSON object containing sha256, kind, entropy, and detected packer.

docs.title: Tool: rekit_ghidra
docs.text:
Arguments: - path (string, required): Absolute path to the binary. - function_name (string, optional): Specific function to decompile (e.g. main).

Response: Decompiled C source code string or error diagnostics.

docs.title: Python Examples
docs.text: Practical scripts demonstrating rekit integration into defensive security pipelines and CI/CD gates.

docs.title: Example 1: Automated Pre-commit Static Gate
docs.text:
import subprocess
import json
import sys

def audit_binary(filepath):
    # Run rekit triage with --json
    cmd = ["python3", "rekit.py", "triage", filepath, "--json"]
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)

    if proc.returncode != 0:
        print(f"Audit failed: {proc.stderr}")
        return False

    data = json.loads(proc.stdout)
    if data.get("packer"):
        print(f"ALERT: Binary is packed with {data['packer']}")
        return False

    print(f"Passed: {filepath} ({data.get('kind')})")
    return True

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if not audit_binary(sys.argv[1]):
        sys.exit(1)

docs.title: Example 2: Batch IOC Hunting
docs.text:
# Scan all downloaded assets in a staging directory
find ./downloads -type f -exec python3 rekit.py iocs {} +

docs.title: Python Quick Start
docs.text: Get up and running with rekit in your terminal or Python scripts.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
rekit has zero mandatory external dependencies. It uses Python's standard library for core triage, strings, and IOC extraction.

git clone https://github.com/Amz34/rekit.git
cd rekit
python3 rekit.py --help

docs.title: 1. Binary Triage
docs.text:
Extract cryptographic hashes, architecture type, section entropy, and detect known packers:

python3 rekit.py triage /bin/ls --json

Output: 

{
  "sha256": "4b227777d4dd1fc61c6f884f48641d02b4d121d3fd328cb08b5531fcacdabf8a",
  "kind": "ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, ARM aarch64",
  "entropy": 6.12,
  "packer": null
}

docs.title: 2. IOC & Credential Extraction
docs.text:
Search strings for URLs, cryptographic private keys, JWTs, IPs, and cloud credentials without detonating code:

python3 rekit.py iocs /path/to/binary_or_bundle

docs.title: 3. Headless Ghidra Decompilation
docs.text:
Invoke Ghidra's headless decompiler to produce C pseudocode:

python3 rekit.py ghidra /bin/ls --func main

docs.title: iocs Heuristics
docs.text:
iocs extracts structured network and credential indicators:

  • IPv4 / IPv6 addresses
  • FQDNs and domains
  • Cryptocurrency wallets (BTC, ETH, XMR)
  • High-entropy JWT strings and cloud keys
  • Tor onion service addresses
